title: delivery-pipeline project config
description: Per-project settings for the delivery-pipeline plugin. Lives at .claude/delivery-pipeline.config.json inside the project repo (checked into git — it holds identifiers, never secrets). Generate it by running the pipeline-init command; every field below has a one-line explanation of what it means and why the pipeline needs it.

maxTicketsPerRun.description: Hard cap on how many tickets one pipeline-sweep pass will touch, across all stages combined. Without this, a sweep against a real backlog would dispatch every matching ticket at once — expensive, hard to review, and easy to overwhelm Jira/git/Render rate limits. Tickets already in progress (qaStatus, then buildStatus) are prioritized over starting new ones (toDoStatus), so in-flight work drains before new work begins. Consider starting lower (e.g. 1-2) for a project's first few sweeps until you've watched it handle a ticket end to end.

maxConcurrentAgents.description: Of the tickets selected for this run, how many get their agent dispatched at the same time. Keeps parallel git worktrees and API calls to Jira/Render bounded even when maxTicketsPerRun is higher.

cloudId.description: Atlassian cloud ID or site hostname (e.g. 'yourteam.atlassian.net'). Identifies which Jira site to query. Get it from mcp__atlassian__getAccessibleAtlassianResources.

projectKey.description: The Jira project key the pipeline watches, e.g. 'SCR'. Only tickets in this project are ever touched.

toDoStatus.description: Status name that means 'nobody has looked at this yet' — the pipeline's entry point. Must be an exact status name in your project's workflow, not a board column label.

planReviewStatus.description: Status used for BOTH human gates: (1) a drafted plan is waiting for your approval, and (2) a QA-passed build is waiting for your merge decision. The pipeline tells these two apart using ticket labels, not the status alone.

buildStatus.description: Status that means 'plan is approved, go build it.' You (or a reviewer) move a ticket here yourself to approve a plan — that drag/click IS the approval mechanism, no separate tool needed.

qaStatus.description: Status that means 'a branch has been built, QA should verify it.' Used both for first-time QA and every re-check after a fix.

doneStatus.description: Terminal status. The pipeline only ever sets this for epics whose child stories have been generated (its job is finished); everything else is left in planReviewStatus for you to close after you merge.

trunkBranch.description: Branch the pipeline branches FROM and eventually targets for the human's merge — e.g. 'master' or 'main'. The pipeline NEVER pushes to this branch directly.

branchPrefix.description: Prefix used to build each feature branch name, with the Jira ticket key appended — e.g. prefix 'feature/' + ticket 'SCR-144' -> 'feature/SCR-144'.

oneCommitPerBranch.description: If true, the engineer agent squashes all its work into a single commit per branch (matches squash-merge workflows). Set false if your repo prefers incremental commit history.

remote.description: Git remote name to push feature branches to.

startCommands.description: One or more shell commands that together bring the app up locally on the feature branch — most repos need more than one (e.g. an API process and a UI process started separately). QA runs all of them, backgrounded, before driving the browser.

localUrl.description: URL the QA agent points the browser (Chrome MCP) at once the dev server is up, e.g. 'http://localhost:3000'.

readyCheckCommand.description: Optional command/curl that returns success once the dev server is actually ready to serve traffic, so QA doesn't race a slow boot. If omitted, QA polls localUrl instead.

testCommand.description: Shell command that runs the automated test suite, e.g. 'yarn jest'. Run by both the engineer (sanity check before handoff) and QA (authoritative check).

mode.description: How the research/triage and QA agents are allowed to verify things against production data. 'direct-readonly': SELECT-only queries straight against prod via the Render Postgres MCP, no size limit. 'single-record-only': direct queries allowed only for single-record lookups (one user, one space); anything broader requires a local restore. 'local-restore-only': every investigation restores a prod dump locally first — the pipeline never queries live prod directly. In all modes, write queries against prod are never permitted.

renderPostgresId.description: Render Postgres instance ID/name to query when mode allows direct queries. Get it from mcp__render__list_postgres_instances.

restoreRunbookPath.description: Path (relative to the project repo) to the doc describing how to pull down and restore a prod dump locally. Required if mode is 'local-restore-only', otherwise used only as a fallback when a direct query can't answer the question.

maxCycles.description: How many fail-and-retry loops (QA finds a problem -> engineer fixes -> QA re-checks) are allowed on one ticket before the pipeline stops looping and escalates to a human instead of continuing to spend cycles.

testAccountStrategy.description: How QA (and research/triage, when reproducing in-browser) gets a safe account to use — never the real reporting user's account/credentials. E.g. a command to provision a quicklogin/test user, or a fixed test-account description.

autoCreate.description: If true, the QA agent opens a pull request (feature branch -> trunkBranch) once a build passes verification, so you get a diff view. It never merges the PR itself.

channel.description: How the pipeline reaches you for the things it can't decide on its own: a plan/build ready for review, or a ticket that's stuck after maxCycles QA failures. Currently only push notification is supported.
